candidate_relations.reason: Schwannomas typically enhance with contrast, arise from cranial nerves, and do not show T1 hyperintensity relative to CSF. The non-enhancing, T1/T2 hyperintense to CSF, well-circumscribed cystic mass in the cerebellomedullary cistern is characteristic of a neurenteric cyst, not a schwannoma.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Schwannoma is a nerve sheath tumor; neurenteric cyst is a congenital endodermal inclusion cyst

candidate_relations.reason: Meningiomas are typically isointense to gray matter on T1/T2, enhance avidly, and often show a dural tail. The non-enhancing, T1 hyperintense to CSF cystic lesion without calcification or enhancement does not fit meningioma.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Meningioma is a meningothelial tumor; neurenteric cyst is a congenital endodermal cyst

candidate_relations.reason: Hemangioblastomas typically show a cyst with an enhancing mural nodule and are associated with von Hippel-Lindau disease. The non-enhancing, T1 hyperintense to CSF, well-circumscribed mass without an enhancing nodule does not fit hemangioblastoma.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Hemangioblastoma is a vascular tumor; neurenteric cyst is a congenital endodermal cyst

case_quality_flags: All three candidates are solid/vascular tumors that do not match the imaging hallmarks of a neurenteric cyst (non-enhancing, T1/T2 hyperintense to CSF, congenital cystic lesion in the posterior fossa cistern).
